clusters.name: Bulimia Nervosa (BN)
items: Recurrent episodes of binge eating (eating in discrete period <=2h definitely larger amount + sense of lack of control) (DSM p.387, Dulcan p.413)
Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain (self-induced vomiting, laxatives, diuretics, fasting, excessive exercise) (DSM p.387, Dulcan p.413)
Self-evaluation unduly influenced by body shape and weight (DSM p.387, Dulcan p.413)

clusters.name: Binge Eating Disorder (BED)
items: Recurrent episodes of binge eating (large amount in discrete period + loss of control) (DSM p.392, Dulcan p.414)

Binge episodes associated with >=3 of: rapid eating, uncomfortably full, eating large amounts when not hungry, eating alone due to embarrassment, feeling disgusted/depressed/guilty (DSM p.392-393, Dulcan p.414)
Marked distress regarding binge eating (DSM p.393, Dulcan p.414)
Absence of recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors (DSM p.393, Dulcan p.414)

criteria.thresholds: BN and BED: average of >=1 episode per week for >=3 months (DSM p.387, p.393, Dulcan p.413-414)
subtypes: BN Current Severity: Mild (1-3 compensatory/wk), Moderate (4-7/wk), Severe (8-13/wk), Extreme (>=14/wk) (DSM p.387, Dulcan p.413)
BED Current Severity: Mild (1-3 binges/wk), Moderate (4-7/wk), Severe (8-13/wk), Extreme (>=14/wk) (DSM p.393, Dulcan p.414)
OSFED: Atypical AN, Subthreshold BN, Subthreshold BED, Purging Disorder, Night Eating Syndrome (DSM p.396, Dulcan p.416)

epidemiology.prevalence: BN: 0.14%-0.3% 12-mo adult, 0.9% lifetime adolescents; BED: 0.44%-1.2% 12-mo adult, 1.6% lifetime adolescents (DSM p.389, p.394, Dulcan p.417)
epidemiology.sex_ratio: BN: 3:1 to 10:1 F:M; BED: 2:1 to 3:1 F:M (DSM p.389, p.394, Dulcan p.417)
epidemiology.onset_age_typical: Late adolescence to young adulthood (ages 15-20 for BN) (DSM p.390, Dulcan p.411, p.417)
comorbidities: Major Depressive Disorder & Bipolar Disorders (DSM p.392, p.396)
Anxiety Disorders (Social Anxiety, GAD) (DSM p.392, p.396)
Substance Use Disorders (>=30% lifetime in BN, AUD/stimulants) (DSM p.392, Dulcan p.417)
epidemiology.prognosis: BN: Chronic or relapsing course; remission >1 yr predicts better long-term outcome (DSM p.390); BED: Higher remission rates than BN or AN (DSM p.395)

etiology.genetic: Heritability 52-62% (BN) and 45-57% (BED); familial transmission of eating, mood, anxiety, and substance disorders (Dulcan p.418, DSM p.390, p.395)
etiology.neurobiology: Shift from Ventral Striatum (impulsivity, mesolimbic dopamine reward) to Dorsal Striatum (compulsivity, Caudate/Putamen habit loop); lisdexamfetamine restores top-down cortical control via striatal neuroplasticity (StahlNeuro p.538-540, p.574-575)
etiology.environmental: Thin-ideal internalization, strict dietary restraint, pubertal maturation fat increases, childhood physical/sexual trauma, family conflict/criticism (DSM p.390, Dulcan p.418-419)

first_line: Family-Based Treatment for BN (FBT-BN) in 3 phases (reestablishing eating, transferring control, adolescent development) (Dulcan p.424)
Fluoxetine (Prozac) 60 mg/day (only FDA-approved SSRI for BN) (StahlKids p.207, Dulcan p.425)
Cognitive-Behavioral Therapy (CBT-BED / CBT-E) in 4 stages (Dulcan p.424, StahlNeuro p.575)
Lisdexamfetamine (Vyvanse) (only FDA-approved medication for BED in adults) (StahlKids p.289, StahlNeuro p.574)
second_line: Topiramate (Topamax) off-label for BED (reduces binges and weight) (StahlKids p.423, StahlNeuro p.575)
Adolescent-Focused Therapy (AFT) or Supportive Psychotherapy (Dulcan p.424-425)
key_side_effects: Fluoxetine: nausea, diarrhea, insomnia, TEAS activation (StahlKids p.207)
Lisdexamfetamine: insomnia, decreased appetite, BP/HR increase, abuse potential (StahlKids p.289)
Topiramate: cognitive fog, sedation, metabolic acidosis via serum bicarbonate reduction (StahlKids p.423)
Bupropion BLACK-BOX CONTRAINDICATION: lowers seizure threshold, strictly forbidden in BN/AN (Dulcan p.718, StahlKids p.83, p.90)
treatment.monitoring: Serum electrolytes (K+, Cl-, HCO3-), ECG (QTc interval), BP, HR, weight/height percentiles, serum bicarbonate baseline and periodic with topiramate (DSM p.391, Dulcan p.613, StahlKids p.423)

items: Eating Disorder Examination (EDE) - gold standard semi-structured interview (Dulcan p.424)
Child EDE - developmentally adapted version for children and young adolescents (Dulcan p.424)
EDE-Q & Parent EDE-Q - self/parent report questionnaire for binge/purge frequency (Dulcan p.424)
PARDI (Pica, ARFID, and Rumination Disorder Interview) (Dulcan p.424)
ESP (Eating Disorder Screen for Primary Care) - 5-question primary care screen (Dulcan p.612)
key_numbers: 5 questions in ESP primary care screening tool (Dulcan p.612)
4 subscales in EDE (Restraint, Eating Concern, Shape Concern, Weight Concern) (Dulcan p.424)
3 phases in FBT-BN treatment model (Dulcan p.424)
4 stages in CBT-E treatment model (Dulcan p.424)

items: Anorexia Nervosa, Binge-Eating/Purging Type - differentiated by significantly low body weight (BMI < 5th percentile in children) (DSM p.381, p.387, Dulcan p.413)
Kleine-Levin Syndrome - neurological disorder with hyperphagia/hypersomnia lacking body shape/weight overvaluation (DSM p.392)
MDD with Atypical Features - overeating without inappropriate compensation or body image preoccupation (DSM p.392, p.395)
Borderline Personality Disorder - binge eating as part of impulsivity criterion (DSM p.392, p.396)
PANS/PANDAS - acute-onset eating restriction or OCD following streptococcal infection (Dulcan p.371)

Medical signs of vomiting/purging: Hypokalemic Hypochloremic Metabolic Alkalosis, Parotid Gland Hypertrophy, Dental Enamel Erosion, Russell's Sign, Mallory-Weiss tears (DSM p.389, p.391, Dulcan p.613)
key_numbers: BMI < 18.5 or < 5th percentile in children distinguishes AN Binge/Purging type from BN (DSM p.381, Dulcan p.413)
25%-33% suicidal ideation/attempt rate in BN (DSM p.391)
25% suicidal ideation rate in BED (DSM p.395)
30% lifetime substance use disorder comorbidity in BN (DSM p.392, Dulcan p.417)

high_yield: BN requires binges + inappropriate compensatory behaviors >=1/week for >=3 months; BED requires binges without compensation >=1/week for >=3 months (DSM p.387, p.393).

Weight is the cardinal differentiator: if body weight is significantly low (BMI < 5th percentile in children), the diagnosis MUST be Anorexia Nervosa Binge-eating/purging type, NOT Bulimia Nervosa (DSM p.381, p.387, Dulcan p.413).
Fluoxetine (Prozac) at 60 mg/day is the ONLY FDA-approved SSRI for Bulimia Nervosa (StahlKids p.207, Dulcan p.425).

Lisdexamfetamine (Vyvanse) is the ONLY FDA-approved medication for Binge Eating Disorder in adults, inducing striatal neuroplasticity to restore top-down cortical control (StahlKids p.289, StahlNeuro p.574-575).

Bupropion (Wellbutrin) is ABSOLUTELY CONTRAINDICATED (Black-Box) in Bulimia Nervosa and Anorexia Nervosa due to lowered seizure threshold and high risk of fatal seizures from electrolyte shifts (Dulcan p.718, StahlKids p.83, p.90).
Family-Based Treatment for Bulimia Nervosa (FBT-BN) in 3 phases is the first-line evidence-based treatment for adolescents with BN (Dulcan p.424).
Purging via vomiting causes Hypokalemic Hypochloremic Metabolic Alkalosis, Parotid Gland Hypertrophy, Dental Enamel Erosion, and Russell's Sign (DSM p.391, Dulcan p.613).

Neurobiologically, binge eating represents a transition from Ventral Striatum (impulsivity/mesolimbic dopamine reward) to Dorsal Striatum (compulsivity/Caudate & Putamen habit loop) (StahlNeuro p.538-540).
